title: Branch multiplicity, component degree, and the double-point tangent criterion
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field], $r\ge2$, and let $D\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ be a reduced closed subscheme of pure dimension one [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $p\in D(k)$ be closed and write $\nu:\coprod_i C_i\to D$ for the componentwise normalization [def-sc-normalization], with $C_i$ smooth proper connected and $e_i=\deg(\nu^*\mathcal O_D(1)|_{C_i})$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. For $q\in\nu^{-1}(p)$, define $b_q$ by
$$\mathfrak m_p\mathcal O_{C_i,q}=\mathfrak m_q^{b_q},\qquad b_q\in\mathbf Z_{\ge1},$$
where $q\in C_i$. Orders are those of the discrete valuation local rings [def-sc-divisor]. Let $t_p$ be the leading coefficient of the eventually linear function $n\mapsto\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{D,p}/\mathfrak m_p^{n+1})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Then
$$t_p=\sum_{q\in\nu^{-1}(p)}b_q,\qquad \sum_{q\in C_i\cap\nu^{-1}(p)}b_q\le e_i.$$
The tangent map from $C_i$ into projective space at $q$ is zero if and only if $b_q\ge2$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. If $t_p=2$ and all these tangent maps are nonzero, then $\nu^{-1}(p)$ has exactly two points $q_1,q_2$, with $b_{q_1}=b_{q_2}=1$. Their one-dimensional tangent images determine projective lines through $p$. They are distinct if and only if
$$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,p}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$$
as complete local $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. If these lines coincide with a line $T$, every ambient linear form vanishing on $T$ pulls back to order at least two at both $q_1$ and $q_2$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{D,p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_p$, $B=(\nu_*\mathcal O_{\coprod C_i})_p$, and $H=\widehat A$. The standard affine charts of the given projective embedding present $D$ by quotients of polynomial rings in finitely many variables, so $D$ is finite type over $k$. The curve completion data apply: $A$ is reduced Noetherian local of dimension one with structural residue field $k$, $B$ is finite over $A$, and $B/A$ has finite length $\delta$. The fibre is finite and nonempty with residue field $k$ at every point. The branch-coordinate node identifies $B\otimes_AH$ with $\prod_q k[[t_q]]$, compatibly with the completed local maps, and identifies $H$ with a subring whose tuples have equal constant coefficients. Each $R_q=\mathcal O_{C_i,q}$ is a DVR. Apply the finite-quotient comparison to $R=A$, $S=B$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$: its local ideals $K_q=\mathfrak mR_q$ satisfy $\mathfrak m_q^{c_q}\subset K_q\subset\mathfrak m_q$. Thus $K_q$ is a nonzero proper ideal in the DVR, uniquely $\mathfrak m_q^{b_q}$ with $b_q\ge1$.

For every $N\ge1$ the same finite-quotient comparison gives
$$B/\mathfrak m^NB\cong\prod_q R_q/\mathfrak m_q^{Nb_q}.$$
Filter each factor by successive powers of its uniformizer. There are exactly $Nb_q$ nonzero quotients, each the residue field $k$ with the structural $A$-action. This simple-module filtration and length additivity give
$$\operatorname{length}_A(B/\mathfrak m^NB)=N\sum_qb_q.$$
Write $s=\sum_qb_q$. No residue-field weights occur, since all residue fields here are $k$.

Apply the finite-colength completion comparison to $A\hookrightarrow B$ and a simple filtration of $B/A$ of length $\delta$. It gives $\mathfrak m^\delta(B/A)=0$. Choose $c=\max(1,\delta)$, so $\mathfrak m^cB\subset A$. Put $h(N)=\operatorname{length}_A(A/\mathfrak m^N)$. For $N>c$, multiplication of this inclusion gives
$$\mathfrak m^NA\subseteq\mathfrak m^NB\subseteq\mathfrak m^{N-c}A\subset A.$$
The exact sequence $0\to A/\mathfrak m^NB\to B/\mathfrak m^NB\to B/A\to0$ and the two quotient surjections therefore give
$$\delta+h(N-c)\le sN\le\delta+h(N).$$
The growth-dimension node applies to the nonzero one-dimensional Noetherian local ring $A$: eventually $h(N)=t_pN+a$ (shifting $N=n+1$ preserves the slope). Divide both inequalities by $N$ and let $N$ tend to infinity. Both outside expressions tend to $t_p$, proving $t_p=s$. This writes out the finite-colength comparison of Stacks 00KB in this particular case.

Fix a component $C_i$ and put $E_i=\sum_{q\in C_i\cap
u^{-1}(p)}b_q[q]$, an effective divisor. Choose an ambient linear form $l$ vanishing at $p$ whose restriction to the image component is not identically zero. Such a form exists: on a chart $X_0(p)
e0$, if every $X_j-p_jX_0$ vanished on the component, it would be contained in the single point $p$, contradicting its dimension one. In the frame $X_0$ the germ $l/X_0$ lies in $\mathfrak m_p$, so its pullback has order at least $b_q$ at every point above $p$. Thus the nonzero pulled-back section of $L_i=
u^*\mathcal O_D(1)|_{C_i}$ belongs to $H^0(C_i,L_i(-E_i))$. Apply the smooth-curve section-degree cap with $A=L_i$, $m=q=1$, $B=E_i$. Its negative-degree vanishing would make this section zero if $\deg E_i>e_i$. Hence $\sum_{q\in C_i\cap
u^{-1}(p)}b_q\le e_i$. If that fibre subset is empty, take $E_i=0$ and any nonzero restricted coordinate section; the same argument proves $0\le e_i$.

At a normalized point $q$, choose the same affine projective chart through $p$ and coordinates $z_j=X_j/X_0-p_j$. Their images generate $\mathfrak m_p$, since $D$ is a closed subscheme of this affine chart. The cotangent map to the DVR is zero exactly when every $z_j$ maps into $\mathfrak m_q^2$, equivalently when $\mathfrak m_pR_q\subseteq\mathfrak m_q^2$, equivalently $b_q\ge2$. Rational tangent/cotangent duality applies to $C_i\to\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ because both points have residue field $k$. It identifies the tangent map with the dual of this coordinate cotangent map. A linear map to the one-dimensional space $\mathfrak m_q/\mathfrak m_q^2$ is zero if and only if its dual is zero (test a nonzero coefficient against a basis functional). This proves the asserted tangent criterion. When $b_q=1$, its dual is injective with one-dimensional image, determining the stated projective line through $p$.

Suppose $t_p=2$ and every tangent map is nonzero. The preceding criterion gives $b_q=1$ at each point, and the multiplicity formula gives exactly two points $q_1,q_2$. Put $P=\{(f,g)\in k[[t_1]]\times k[[t_2]]:f(0)=g(0)\}$. The completed normalization embedding of Step 1 factors as $H\hookrightarrow P$. The axes node identifies $P\cong k[[U,V]]/(UV)$. Its maximal ideal is generated by $(t_1,0)$ and $(0,t_2)$, and its square consists of pairs of orders at least two. Consequently $\mathfrak n_P/\mathfrak n_P^2\cong k^2$, with coordinates the two linear coefficients. The power-series structure node and the complete-local quotient node show that $P$ is Noetherian complete local with structural residue field $k$. The same properties for $H$ were supplied in Step 1.

proof.text: Assume the two projective tangent lines are distinct. Their corresponding one-dimensional vector subspaces in $T_{\mathbf P^{r-1}/k,p}$ are distinct, so their nonzero generating tangent vectors are linearly independent. By rational tangent/cotangent duality, the ambient cotangent map to the two branch cotangents $k\oplus k$ is surjective: its two component linear functionals are independent. This map factors through $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2$, hence through $\mathfrak m_H/\mathfrak m_H^2$. Indeed completion modulo powers and the local-completion maximal-ideal formula identify these latter cotangent spaces canonically. Under Step 6 the resulting map $\mathfrak m_H/\mathfrak m_H^2\to\mathfrak n_P/\mathfrak n_P^2$ is exactly the map of the inclusion $H\hookrightarrow P$. That inclusion is a continuous local $k$-algebra homomorphism: residues agree and powers of its maximal ideal map into the corresponding powers in $P$. Apply complete-local cotangent surjectivity with coefficient base $C=k$, $R=H$, $S=P$. All rings are complete Noetherian local with residue $k$ by Steps 1 and 6. The inclusion is surjective, hence $H=P\cong k[[U,V]]/(UV)$.

Conversely, suppose $H\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as complete local $k$-algebras. The split-node normalization node applies: $A$ is reduced, essentially of finite type over $k$, one-dimensional and has this specified completion by Step 1. It identifies the two completed branch maps with $u\mapsto t,v\mapsto0$ and $u\mapsto0,v\mapsto t$. Thus the map from the cotangent space of $H$ to the two branch cotangents is the coordinate isomorphism $k^2\to k^2$. Completion modulo powers and the local maximal-ideal formula identify it with the map from $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2$. Ambient affine coordinates generate $\mathfrak m_A$, so the ambient cotangent surjects onto this space and then onto the two branch cotangents. By tangent/cotangent duality, the two tangent vectors are linearly independent in the ambient tangent space. Hence their projective lines are distinct. This includes the case that the two points lie on the same global component.

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node), varieties.tex Tag 0C3V; tangent duality Tags 0B2E, 0B2F.

proof.text: Finally suppose the lines coincide with $T$. For a linear form $l$ vanishing on $T$, its ratio $l/X_0$ has value zero at $p$, and its differential annihilates the tangent direction of $T$. Both branch tangent maps have this image. Their pullbacks therefore have zero value and zero linear coefficient, so they lie in $\mathfrak m_{q_1}^2$ and $\mathfrak m_{q_2}^2$. This is precisely order at least two in the local frame $X_0$. The assertion includes an identically zero pullback, whose order is infinite. All calculations concern the first coefficient and work in every characteristic; no differentiation of a higher power was used.
